subject: error handling should be on doubles, not vars

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: error handling should be on doubles, not vars
parts:
On 3/5/13 2:29 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> Another issue is check_simplex, which is doing it's check directly on the vars. It's much faster to copy the values to
> doubles and then do the check on those. In fact, looking at check_simplex right now it does:
>
> if (fabs(1.0 - theta.sum()) > CONSTRAINT_TOLERANCE) {
> ...
> }
>
> which not only computes the sum using vars, it also avoids using the faster sum vari because it calls theta.sum()
> instead of sum(theta). This will hurt a lot for large simplexes.

Good catch.

I just fixed it. [Well, I at least made it more efficient
for variable simplexes -- there's a bit more that could be
done to cut out the intermediate allocation, so it's still
going to be slower than just incrementing lp__ by log(theta[i])].

It's not just the computation and use of .sum(), it's the
fact that it's going to pile a ton of extra work onto the
auto-dif stack. The basic .sum() is fine for doubles.

I just added a to-do item for Daniel (what power!) to review all
of our code and fix this wherever else it needs to be done.
We'd decided to do the tests at the double level before, but I
don't think Daniel's gotten to the multivariate distros yet.

- Bob
